props.title: It Happened One Night
props.initialSlug: A runaway heiress meets a reporter.

sections.content: It Happened One Night revolutionized romantic comedy and created the blueprint for the modern screwball genre. Frank Capra's masterpiece pairs Clark Gable's roguish reporter with Claudette Colbert's runaway heiress, establishing the "opposites attract" dynamic that would influence decades of films like When Harry Met Sally (1989) and Pretty Woman (1990). The film swept all five major Academy Awards - a feat not repeated until One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (1975). Its famous "Walls of Jericho" blanket scene and hitchhiking sequence have been referenced countless times, while Gable's undressing scene allegedly hurt undershirt sales when he appeared bare-chested.

sections.content: The film's road trip structure became a template for romantic comedies, showing how forced proximity and shared adventures can spark romance. This influence is evident in films like The Sure Thing (1985) and Midnight Run (1988), though the latter adds action elements. The chemistry between Gable and Colbert set the standard for the romantic comedy power couple - their initial antagonism melting into attraction through witty banter and shared experiences. This dynamic echoes through The African Queen (1951) and modern hits like While You Were Sleeping (1995). SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Cinema

While Depression-era audiences connected with its themes of class division and economic struggle, It Happened One Night remains startlingly modern in its treatment of gender dynamics and social commentary. The film's influence can be seen in contemporary romantic road movies like Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987) and Something Wild (1986). Its DNA is particularly evident in films that pair seemingly mismatched couples from different social classes, from Notting Hill (1999) to Silver Linings Playbook (2012).
